mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST QoQ change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY and HOUST declines by more than 10% QoQ.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as firms pass costs to consumers and maintain earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of three consecutive months with UNRATE below 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.5% in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals expanding manufacturing output, which correlates with higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > previous month + 0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of four consecutive months with INDPRO rising by at least 0.5% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline of more than 1% in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals a coordinated weakening in consumer demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < -1% AND RSAFS monthly change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both PAYEMS and RSAFS decline by more than 1% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid reduction in the federal funds rate by more than 0.75 percentage points within a single month signals an emergency monetary easing, which immediately boosts risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive following a single-month FEDFUNDS decline of more than 0.75 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment (PAYEMS) increase of less than 50,000 while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises signals a deterioration in labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < 50,000 AND UNRATE monthly change > 0.1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS increases by less than 50,000 and UNRATE rises in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the housing starts index (HOUST) below 900,000 for six consecutive months signals a prolonged housing downturn, which reduces construction-related economic activity and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when HOUST remains below 900,000 for six consecutive months.
